risks.note: The industry has over 79 players and capacity far above market demand, with existing market overcapacity stated at around 100% and new barrel plants still emerging in the Western and Southern regions. A large number of unorganised players with low overheads, low entry barriers and locational advantages compete against a highly price-sensitive customer base, keeping pricing pressure permanent in the Company's largest segment by turnover.
risks.risk: Structural overcapacity and fragmented competition in the 210L mild-steel drum industry

risks.note: Escalating and volatile steel prices drive up the cost of MS drums relative to HDPE drums, and the division faces intense competition from alternate packaging solutions including Intermediate Bulk Containers, collapsible bins, HDPE and reconditioned drums. Elevated crude and commodity prices are flagged as a pressure on margins.
risks.risk: Raw-material price volatility and substitution risk in Industrial Packaging

risks.note: The business depends on imported base oils and specialty additives, exposing it to supply chain disruption and foreign exchange fluctuation, with limited availability and rising cost of lithium-based raw materials specifically flagged. Profitability in the division faced pressure during the year from intense competition and the scarcity of certain base oil grades.
risks.risk: Crude, base oil and additive price volatility plus critical input scarcity in Greases & Lubricants

risks.note: Aggressive pricing by large OMCs and multinational lubricant manufacturers creates significant pricing pressure on operating margins. The Company has comparatively lower brand visibility in retail lubricants, limited OEM approvals in certain categories, and competitors are aggressively increasing branding, digital marketing and OEM partnership investment.
risks.risk: Competitive and brand-position weakness against MNCs and PSU Oil Marketing Companies in automotive lubricants

risks.note: The division's revenue base reflects a high reliance on Government and PSU clients, exposing the business to significant customer concentration risk. Brand recall in the competitive retail leisure and MICE segments remains subdued versus private-sector OTAs, leaving the business vulnerable to margin pressure and industry cyclicality including geopolitical shocks, airline capacity rationalisation and shifting commission structures.
risks.risk: Customer concentration on Government and PSU clients in Travel & Vacations

risks.note: Refrigeration operations are highly energy-intensive, making profitability exceptionally sensitive to electricity tariff hikes that cannot always be passed to customers. The division relies heavily on a few large customers and faces capacity underutilisation during seasonal demand fluctuations tied to agricultural cycles, causing revenue volatility.
risks.risk: Customer concentration and energy-cost sensitivity in Cold Chain

risks.note: The entry of 9-10 new competitors has compressed profitability margins and equipment utilisation, market share has decreased, and overall market size is trending down on lower processing rates and stagnant volume. Management states the business seems economically unviable to Balmer Lawrie and the Board has decided to discontinue it. A further long-run risk is adoption of modern refinery technologies that reduce oil sludge generation.
risks.risk: Structural decline and exit of the Refinery & Oil Field Services business

risks.note: The year was shaped by escalation of the Gulf Crisis, rising global tariff protectionism and supply-chain disruption, with geopolitics and national security overtaking economic efficiency as drivers of global trade. Logistics divisions contended with global supply chain disruptions, severe ocean and air freight market volatility, port congestion and shifting trade regulations, alongside heavy dependence on external shipping lines, airlines and transport providers for execution.

currentContext.expansion: Industrial Packaging operates six manufacturing plants pan-India including a state-of-the-art facility at Navi Mumbai; the modernisation of the Chittoor plant has been completed and will enable an enhanced product basket, while IP-Silvassa underwent a plant layout modification necessitated by a road-widening project without affecting day-to-day operations. Following closure of the Kolkata drum manufacturing plant, the Eastern Region market is served through a local Tolling Business Model. Process and product upgrades under way across Industrial Packaging include introduction of SDB (Standard Domed Bottom) drums at Silvassa, Chittoor and Asaoti, conversion from 648 to 642 diameter lids across all IP plants (a stated 7% steel saving), direct application of special paint over Cold Rolled steel without surface treatment at the Taloja plant, and conversion of fuel from High-Speed Diesel to Light Diesel Oil / LPG at the Silvassa, Chittoor and Chennai plants. In Cold Chain, five Temperature Controlled Warehouses operate at Hyderabad, Rai, Vijayawada, Patalganga and Bhubaneshwar supported by 29 real-time monitored refrigerated vehicles; the Vijayawada TCW was operationalised during FY 2025-26 and drove the division's revenue growth, and a new TCW facility in Kolkata is currently under development to strengthen the Eastern India presence. In Logistics, the Company is entering Rail Logistics and has proposed Gati Shakti Cargo Terminals. Solar plants have been commissioned at the Mumbai logistics facility and subsequently at Chennai, and the Mumbai facility has achieved zero liquid discharge through its Sewage Treatment Plant, with further renewable-energy sourcing and storage options being evaluated as part of a medium-term sustainability roadmap. The Board has decided to discontinue the Refinery & Oil Field Services business, accepting no new orders and completing existing ones, freeing up capital and management bandwidth for higher-growth verticals.

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- The industry has over 79 players and capacity far above market demand, with existing market overcapacity stated at around 100% and new barrel plants still emerging in the Western and Southern regions. A large number of unorganised players with low overheads, low entry barriers and locational advantages compete against a highly price-sensitive customer base, keeping pricing pressure permanent in the Company's largest segment by turnover.
- Escalating and volatile steel prices drive up the cost of MS drums relative to HDPE drums, and the division faces intense competition from alternate packaging solutions including Intermediate Bulk Containers, collapsible bins, HDPE and reconditioned drums. Elevated crude and commodity prices are flagged as a pressure on margins.
- The business depends on imported base oils and specialty additives, exposing it to supply chain disruption and foreign exchange fluctuation, with limited availability and rising cost of lithium-based raw materials specifically flagged. Profitability in the division faced pressure during the year from intense competition and the scarcity of certain base oil grades.
- Aggressive pricing by large OMCs and multinational lubricant manufacturers creates significant pricing pressure on operating margins. The Company has comparatively lower brand visibility in retail lubricants, limited OEM approvals in certain categories, and competitors are aggressively increasing branding, digital marketing and OEM partnership investment.
- The division's revenue base reflects a high reliance on Government and PSU clients, exposing the business to significant customer concentration risk. Brand recall in the competitive retail leisure and MICE segments remains subdued versus private-sector OTAs, leaving the business vulnerable to margin pressure and industry cyclicality including geopolitical shocks, airline capacity rationalisation and shifting commission structures.
- Refrigeration operations are highly energy-intensive, making profitability exceptionally sensitive to electricity tariff hikes that cannot always be passed to customers. The division relies heavily on a few large customers and faces capacity underutilisation during seasonal demand fluctuations tied to agricultural cycles, causing revenue volatility.
- The entry of 9-10 new competitors has compressed profitability margins and equipment utilisation, market share has decreased, and overall market size is trending down on lower processing rates and stagnant volume. Management states the business seems economically unviable to Balmer Lawrie and the Board has decided to discontinue it. A further long-run risk is adoption of modern refinery technologies that reduce oil sludge generation.
- The year was shaped by escalation of the Gulf Crisis, rising global tariff protectionism and supply-chain disruption, with geopolitics and national security overtaking economic efficiency as drivers of global trade. Logistics divisions contended with global supply chain disruptions, severe ocean and air freight market volatility, port congestion and shifting trade regulations, alongside heavy dependence on external shipping lines, airlines and transport providers for execution.

themes.title: Logistics, ports & supply-chain formalization
themes.need: E-commerce, quick-commerce and GST-driven warehousing consolidation plus a 1P->3P shift drive an integrated-logistics up-cycle. DELHIVERY hit early FCF (>1B parcels, Express +46% rev) with Express targeting 16-18% margin; CONCOR/GATEWAY/JSWINFRA on rail/ports; ALLCARGO/MAHLOG/TVSSCS/VRLLOG on 3PL/road; BLUEDART/TCIEXP/WCIL/SNOWMAN on express + cold-chain; DELHIVERY/SHADOWFAX on quick-commerce fulfilment. Q1FY27's clearest turnaround datapoint: MAHLOG swung to a +INR 25.4cr PAT from a -INR 10.8cr loss on +23% revenue, with B2B Express (Rivigo) gross margin turning +6% from -3.8% and its EBITDA loss cut to -INR 1.6cr from -INR 11.8cr, guided to EBITDA breakeven within FY27, while Contract Logistics grew 26% with margin diluted only ~46bps on new-site start-up costs (opening a site almost every week).
themes.driver: Express/quick-commerce volume momentum; warehousing leasing; port/rail throughput; operating-leverage inflection.

hero.oneLiner: Balmer Lawrie & Co. Ltd. is a diversified Mini-Ratna Category-I public sector enterprise, market leader in 210L mild-steel industrial drums and specialty greases, operating across industrial packaging, greases & lubricants, leather chemicals, logistics and travel.
